sections.title: Artigos definidos e indefinidos
sections.note:
We begin with articles because they are present in all speech and we need them whenever we use nouns.
There are 4 definite articles and 4 indefinite articles. Definite articles are used before a noun whose identity is known and correspond to the English word "the". Indefinite articles are used before a noun whose identity is not known and correspond to "a" or "an" (plural: "some").

The house is big.

sections.title: Preposições
sections.note:
Prepositions are words that connect 2 words in a clause, expressing grammatical relations between them. Remember that prepositions are very arbitrary, and therefore very hard to translate from one language to another.
The prepositions a, de, em and por merge with the definite articles that follow them, e.g. por + o = pelo (for the / through the). The preposition em also merges with indefinite articles: em + um = num (in a).

sections.title: Substantivos
sections.note:
Nouns are the words we use to name things, such as objects, living creatures, feelings, emotions and professions. Every noun in the list is given with its definite article and grouped by topic.
There are 2 genders in Portuguese: masculine and feminine. As a rule of thumb, nouns ending in -o are masculine and nouns ending in -a are feminine, but there are exceptions, and many nouns end in other letters.
How to form the plural:
• Words ending in a vowel add -s: o tempo → os tempos.
• Words ending in a consonant add -es: a vez → as vezes.
• Words ending in -m replace it with -ns: o homem → os homens.
• Words ending in -l replace it with -is: o final → os finais.
• Words ending in -ão replace it with -ões: a relação → as relações.
